explain.say: The Quran is the holy book of Islam, revealed in Arabic over about 23 years. It has 114 chapters, called surahs, and many Muslims learn parts of it by heart.
Muslim life rests on the Five Pillars: the declaration of faith, prayer five times a day, giving to the poor, fasting in Ramadan, and the pilgrimage to Mecca.
Muslims pray in a mosque, facing the Kaaba in Mecca. A niche called the mihrab shows the direction, the call to prayer rings out from the minaret, and on Fridays the community prays together.
Most Muslims are Sunni, and a smaller group, roughly one in ten, are Shia. They share the Quran and the Five Pillars, and celebrate Eid al-Fitr after Ramadan and Eid al-Adha during the Hajj.

b: Leadership through Ali and his descendants

draw.a: One God, the Quran, the Five Pillars, the two Eids

faq.q: What are the Five Pillars of Islam?
faq.a: The Five Pillars are the duties at the heart of Muslim life: Shahada, the declaration of faith; Salah, prayer five times a day; Zakat, giving to those in need; Sawm, fasting in Ramadan; and Hajj, the pilgrimage to Mecca once in a lifetime if able.
asks: What are the five duties of a Muslim?

faq.q: Why do Muslims fast during Ramadan?
faq.a: Fasting in Ramadan is commanded in the Quran and is one of the Five Pillars. From dawn to sunset Muslims go without food and drink to grow closer to God, practise self-control and gratitude, and feel for people who are hungry. Children, the sick, the elderly and travellers do not have to fast.

Allah is the Arabic word for God. Muslims believe Allah is the one God, the creator of everything, merciful and just, and the same God worshipped by Abraham, Moses and Jesus. Arabic-speaking Christians also say Allah for God.
asks: Is Allah the same as God?

faq.a: Muslims believe the Prophet Muhammad, born in Mecca about 570 CE, was the final messenger of God. From about 610 CE he received the revelations of the Quran, and in 622 CE he moved to Medina, where the first Muslim community grew.
asks: Who is the prophet of Islam?
Tell me about the Prophet Muhammad

faq.a: The Quran is the holy book of Islam. Muslims believe it is the word of God revealed in Arabic to the Prophet Muhammad through the angel Jibril, or Gabriel. It has 114 surahs, and is recited in prayer.
asks: What is the Muslim holy book?
How many chapters are in the Quran?

faq.a: A mosque is a place of prayer and community. Worshippers take off their shoes, wash in a ritual called wudu, and pray in rows facing Mecca, led by an imam. The main weekly gathering is the Friday prayer, called Jumu'ah.
asks: What do Muslims do at the mosque?

faq.a: The Kaaba is the cube-shaped building at the centre of the Great Mosque in Mecca, the holiest place in Islam. Muslims believe Abraham and his son Ishmael built it for the worship of one God. Muslims everywhere face it when they pray, which unites them in one direction.
asks: Why do Muslims pray facing Mecca?
What is the black cube in Mecca?

faq.a: Muslims pray five times a day: at dawn, midday, afternoon, sunset and night. The call to prayer, the adhan, announces each time. Prayer involves standing, bowing and kneeling with the forehead touching the ground.

The Hajj is the pilgrimage to Mecca that every adult Muslim who is able should make once in their life. Millions gather each year, wear simple white clothes, walk around the Kaaba, and stand in prayer at Arafat.
asks: What is the pilgrimage to Mecca?
Why do Muslims go to Mecca?

faq.q: What is the difference between Sunni and Shia Muslims?
faq.a: The split began over who should lead the Muslim community after the Prophet Muhammad died. Sunnis, about 85 to 90 percent of Muslims, accepted elected caliphs; Shia Muslims believe leadership belonged to his cousin and son-in-law Ali and his descendants. Both share the Quran and the Five Pillars.

Muslims celebrate two Eids. Eid al-Fitr marks the end of Ramadan with prayers, new clothes, gifts and charity. Eid al-Adha, during the Hajj, remembers Abraham's willingness to obey God, and meat is shared with family and the poor.
Halal means permitted. Halal food follows Islamic law: no pork or alcohol, and meat from animals slaughtered in a set way with God's name said. The opposite, haram, means forbidden.
asks: Why do Muslims not eat pork?

faq.q: Why do some Muslim women wear a hijab?
faq.a: Many Muslim women wear a hijab, a headscarf, as an act of faith and modesty taught in the Quran and tradition. Practice varies: some cover their hair, some do not, and it is often a personal choice.
asks: Why do Muslims cover their heads?

faq.q: Why are there no pictures of the Prophet in Islam?
faq.a: Most Muslims do not make images of the Prophet Muhammad or other prophets, out of deep respect and to avoid anything that could lead to worshipping images. Islamic art instead uses beautiful calligraphy and geometric patterns.
asks: Why can you not draw the Prophet Muhammad?
Why does Islamic art use patterns?

facts: Muslims numbered about 2 billion in 2020, about 25.6 percent of the world (Pew Research).
The Quran has 114 surahs, or chapters.
The Hijra, the Prophet Muhammad's move from Mecca to Medina in 622 CE, marks year one of the Islamic calendar.
The Islamic calendar is lunar, so Ramadan comes about 11 days earlier each year.
Indonesia has the largest Muslim population of any country.

quiz.show: Giving to those in need is…
quiz.why: Zakat is the duty to give a share of one's wealth, usually 2.5 percent of savings each year, to those in need.

quiz.say: A Muslim in London is ready to pray. Which way does she face?
quiz.why: Muslims everywhere face the Kaaba in Mecca, a direction called the qibla, shown in a mosque by the mihrab.

wrong.0: Early Muslims briefly faced Jerusalem, but the qibla became Mecca.
wrong.1: The direction is to Mecca, not to the sun.
wrong.3: There is a set direction: the qibla.

quiz.why: Twelve lunar months make about 354 days, so Ramadan moves about 11 days earlier each year and passes through every season over about 33 years.

wrong.0: The date comes from the lunar calendar and the sighting of the new moon, not a choice.
wrong.2: The Islamic calendar is separate from the Christian one.
wrong.3: Ramadan is tied to the moon, not to the solstice.
